title: [D2 Context] Registrable-domain normalization via the Public Suffix List
summary: The Public Suffix List is loaded and the registrable domain is derived in the engine. sql/migrations/0008_public_suffix_list.sql adds helena_reference_public_suffix (one snapshot at a time, one row per match key) and helena_reference_public_suffix_load (one row per attempt, three statuses, three typed failure reasons), plus four signal-layer objects that turn a domain entity value into its public suffix and registrable domain by an equi-join against the rules. src/helena/enrichment.py stops being a placeholder: it fetches, parses and replaces a snapshot, and records the attempt either way; scripts/load_public_suffix_list.py is what runs it on a schedule and is the one place the source URL is written.
assumption_validated: That the Public Suffix List algorithm -- longest match, wildcards, exceptions, a default rule -- can run inside RisingWave as a streaming join rather than as Python on the stream path, and that its answers are the publisher's answers. Both hold. The engine takes a set-returning function that generates a name's candidate suffixes from its own label count (generate_series(0, cardinality(labels)) as a column-dependent SRF survives into a materialized view; the same call with constant arguments is planned as a nested-loop join and is refused), an equi-join of those candidates against the rules, an aggregate that expresses exception precedence and longest-match in one CASE, and a LEFT join that keeps a name whatever happened to it. Correctness is not this session's reasoning: the publisher's own 77 checkPublicSuffix vectors are committed verbatim and every one of them agrees, run end to end -- name to DNS query to capture to normalized event to entity row to registrable domain. The vectors cover mixed case, a leading dot, an unlisted TLD, a TLD whose only rule is a wildcard, wildcards with exceptions, four-label US K12 names and IDN labels in both Unicode and punycode form.
makes_buildable: The enrichment join (D3) can now compare scope. helena_signal_context_domains gives it a domain entity row with the name as observed in `entity_value` (unchanged, which is what ADR-0009 fixes the Netify join on) and `registrable_domain` beside it for the comparison ADR-0009 says must not sit in front of that join. The ThreatFox loader has a worked example of everything it needs: a snapshot-versioned reference table, an insert-then-delete replacement, a load table whose failures are typed and countable, a redacted source URL as provenance, and a measured 500-row-chunk INSERT that is 13x faster than executemany. helena.enrichment is no longer a placeholder module, so a second loader is a function beside this one rather than a decision about where loaders live.

verification.detail: 550 passed in 1025s, whole suite, against a real RisingWave 3.0.3 started from bin/. 37 of the 550 are tests/test_enrichment.py, 36 of them new. Every assertion about the new tables and views executes SQL against a throwaway schema on that engine, over records put through the real normalizer and rules put through the real loader -- nothing asserts on SQL text. Two of the 37 fetch the live list from publicsuffix.org and passed against it: one checks the published format still parses (10 321 rules, both sections, wildcards and exceptions present), the other asserts the committed 34-rule extract offers the join the same rules as the full list for every name the suite tests, so the extract is a sufficient subset rather than a convenient one. Both skip rather than fail when the machine cannot reach the publisher. Three mutation checks were run outside the suite: replacing exception precedence with a plain longest-match breaks 4 of the 77 vectors (city.kobe.jp, www.ck and two more); removing the name-validity filter breaks the four-states test and the vectors; removing the wildcard guard breaks NOTHING in the vectors, which is why test_a_wildcard_needs_a_label_to_consume was added and asserts the suffix length -- it fails under that mutation (ck reads 2 labels instead of 1, kobe.jp reads 3 instead of 1).

escalations.detail: A source is now fetched and stored that was not before: publicsuffix.org/list/public_suffix_list.dat. concept/05-threat-intelligence.md lists the Public Suffix List in the source catalogue but below the two accepted rows, i.e. inside the block the note calls deferred -- while giving it an empty 'Maps to' cell and no tier, which is what the note means by it not being an enrichment source at all. prd task 15 instructs the load, so it was done; the operator may want the catalogue to say explicitly that the normalization row is not governed by the same 'deferred' as the feeds below it. No credential is involved (the list is open) and no runtime dependency was added -- the fetch is urllib from the standard library, because docs/decisions/0002-dependency-set.md keeps requests and httpx deliberately absent.

helena.versions.VersionSet has eight dimensions and none of them is a normalization snapshot. `enrichment_snapshot_version` is the feed snapshot an enrichment join matched against; the Public Suffix List snapshot is not that, and a registrable domain that reached an assessment would have no dimension to record what decided it. Nothing cites one yet, so nothing is wrong today. The derived row carries `public_suffix_snapshot_version` so the fact is available; adding a ninth dimension to the version set is a contract change and therefore the operator's, not a session's. This becomes real in the increment that first renders a registrable domain to an agent.

deferred: An ICANN-only derivation. Both sections are loaded and both are used, because that is what separates shared infrastructure -- one.workers.dev and two.workers.dev are different registrants, and data/threatfox/domains_recent.json actually contains *.workers.dev names. `section` is on every rule row so an ICANN-only variant can be added when something needs one; a second derivation with no reader would be a view with one caller and no way to be wrong.

Case folding a non-ASCII name. Measured: RisingWave 3.0.3's lower() is ASCII-only -- lower('ÉX') is 'Éx' -- so an uppercase U-label is not folded. The sample carries no non-ASCII name at all, so this is unexercised rather than known-harmless, and it is recorded in the migration head rather than worked around.

Detecting a bracketed IPv6 literal as an invalid name. Two validity rules are implemented (an empty label; a rightmost label that is all digits, which catches an IPv4 literal in a URI host part) and both are from the domain-name grammar. `[::1]` is not caught; measured over data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl, no URI host is an address literal of either kind, so a third rule would be guessing at a case no input has.
A registrable domain for `url` entities. A URL's host part is already a `domain` entity of its own (0007), so the derivation reaches it there and a second one would be two answers to one question.

A scheduler. 'On its own schedule' is scripts/load_public_suffix_list.py run by cron, a timer or a hand. Nothing in this repository schedules anything and a scheduler with its own state would be a second store (concept/instruction.md §2).

A configuration variable for the list's URL. concept/05 opens with 'adding a source is a governed decision, not a configuration convenience', and a source URL in the environment is that convenience. It is a constant in the script, the loader takes it as an argument, and the package holds no URL at all -- which tests/test_broker.py::test_no_module_in_the_package_holds_a_broker_address already enforces.

A decision record under docs/. The argument -- why normalization and not enrichment, why a join and not a function, why both sections, what the four statuses mean and what is not detected -- is in the head of sql/migrations/0008_public_suffix_list.sql, which is where a reader of the SQL looks, plus a new docs/runbook.md §9 for the operational half. Same choice tasks 13 and 14 made, and prds/CONTEXT.md §5 asks not to grow docs/ where the code and the report carry it. ADR-0009 forward-references this task and its statement is still exactly true, so it was not edited.
lessons: task 15: A set-returning function whose argument depends on a column survives into a RisingWave 3.0.3 streaming plan; the same function with constant arguments does not. `generate_series(0, cardinality(labels))` in the SELECT list of a plain view, with a materialized view over it, works and backfills. `FROM names, generate_series(0, 10) AS g(i)` is planned as a streaming nested-loop join and refused outright. `unnest(ARRAY[0,1,...])` in the SELECT list also works. So a per-row fan-out is available, and it does not need an arbitrary depth constant -- which is what let the candidate generation here have no limit to outgrow.

task 15: Dynamic array slicing works in RisingWave 3.0.3 -- `a[cardinality(a)-n+1 : cardinality(a)]` with n from a column -- and an out-of-range slice CLAMPS rather than raising or returning NULL. `(string_to_array('a.b','.'))[-8:2]` gives the whole array. That makes a bounds error look like a plausible answer, so any slice with a computed start needs the invariant that keeps it in range asserted somewhere a test can fail.

task 15: `substring(x FROM 'regex')` is parsed as `substring(x FROM int)` in RisingWave 3.0.3 and fails with 'Parse error: integer invalid digit'. Use `regexp_match(x, pattern)` (returns an array, index it with [1]) or the `~` operator, which does work. Negative `split_part` indices work too.

task 15: Between the INSERTs and the DELETE of a snapshot replacement there MUST be a FLUSH. Without it the DELETE scans a state the INSERTs have not reached and removes every row -- new snapshot included -- leaving an empty table and raising nothing. Measured: the replacement test read back zero rows. Insert-then-flush-then-delete-by-old-version is the order, and it is chosen for what its half-done state looks like: a superset of the rules for a moment rather than an empty list.

task 15: A 500-row multi-row INSERT is 13x faster than psycopg's executemany against RisingWave 3.0.3 -- 1.2 s versus 15.9 s for the list's 10 781 rows. The round trip is the cost, not the write. Worth knowing before the ThreatFox loader writes 3 375 rows on every refresh.

task 15: The publisher's own checkPublicSuffix vectors do NOT cover the wildcard guard. Mutation-checked: removing `name_label_count > candidate_label_count` from the wildcard branch leaves all 77 passing, because not one vector is a name equal to a wildcard rule's parent. External test vectors are worth far more than hand-written ones and are still not a coverage argument -- mutate the thing and see whether anything notices.

task 15: The algorithm's default rule `*` is stored as an actual row rather than expressed as a COALESCE. That is what makes `no rule matched` mean `the table is empty` and nothing else, so `missing` and `no_match` stay apart in the derivation, and it is also what carries `snapshot_version` onto every derived row through the join. A COALESCE would have produced a plausible answer with no provenance.

task 15: A rule with non-ASCII labels is loaded twice, once as published and once punycoded, because a name may be observed in either form and the join is on bytes. `'xn--' + label.encode('punycode').decode('ascii')` per non-ASCII label is the whole of it and needs no dependency; it reproduces the published IDN suffixes exactly (公司.cn -> xn--55qx5d.cn). 459 of the 10 321 rules are affected.

task 15: `helena_signal_context_entities` is a materialized view, so a test cannot insert a name into it. The way to drive the derivation with names of a test's own is task 12's technique one level up: the layer fixture's first record (udp.0) is a real DNS lookup, and replacing `dns.queries` with one entry per name -- keeping the rest of the observation, `rcode` included -- puts 77 names through the real path in one capture. Rebuilding the `dns` object from scratch quarantines the record with `dns.rcode: Field required`.
task 15: RisingWave reports a table as `BASE TABLE` in information_schema.tables, not `TABLE`. The existing tests only ever asserted on views, so this is new ground for the shape assertions.
failed_approaches: task 15: A `LIKE '%.' || suffix` join from names to rules. It is a non-equi join, which RisingWave refuses as a 'streaming nested-loop join' -- the same refusal 0002 recorded. The whole candidate-suffix construction exists because of it; do not try to shortcut back to a suffix predicate.

task 15: `FROM names, generate_series(0, 10) AS g(i)` to generate candidates. Fine in a plain view, refused the moment a materialized view is built over it, for the same nested-loop reason. Making the series bound a column expression is what fixes it, and it removes the constant as a bonus.

task 15: Replacing a snapshot with delete-then-insert, and with insert-then-delete without a FLUSH between them. The second leaves the table empty and raises nothing (measured). The first would leave every name its own public suffix for the duration of the load.

task 15: Nothing else was tried and abandoned. One thing not to repeat: the throwaway engine for this session was started by hand with an explicit workdir and left running, which conftest.py then reused; `pgrep -x risingwave` is how to check for it, never `pgrep -f`.
next_session_should_know: Migration 0008 adds seven objects. Two tables with a writer -- `helena_reference_public_suffix` (snapshot_version, rule, suffix, is_wildcard, is_exception, section; PK (rule, suffix)) and `helena_reference_public_suffix_load` (attempted_at, source_url, status, snapshot_version, rule_count, failure_reason, failure_detail; PK (attempted_at, source_url)) -- plus `helena_reference_public_suffix_load_counts`, a plain view mirroring helena_ingest_quarantine_counts. Then four signal objects: `helena_signal_domain_suffix_candidates` and `helena_signal_domain_public_suffix` (plain intermediates), `helena_signal_domain_registrable` (materialized: observed_name, normalized_name, name_label_count, public_suffix_label_count, public_suffix, registrable_domain, registrable_domain_status, public_suffix_snapshot_version) and `helena_signal_context_domains` (plain: every entity column except fingerprint_algorithm, plus the five derived ones). Seven things to build on rather than rediscover. (1) `entity_value` is untouched and must stay so -- ADR-0009 fixes the one existing feed's join on the name AS OBSERVED, and the registrable domain is a column beside it for a different question, never a rewrite of it. (2) `registrable_domain_status` has four values and they are four different things: `derived`, `name_is_a_public_suffix` (nothing is missing; there is nothing there), `invalid_name` (the list was consulted and refused the name) and `list_not_loaded` (the reference table is empty -- `missing`, never `no_match`). A consumer that collapses any two of them into a NULL breaks concept/instruction.md §2. (3) The table holds exactly one snapshot at a time and the derivation GROUPs BY snapshot_version rather than taking max(), so a two-snapshot table produces two rows per name and fails the one-row-per-name assertion loudly instead of being silently decided by whichever digest sorts higher. (4) tests/test_context.py::test_every_signal_object_declares_what_it_is is still a prefix query and now names seven objects; adding one to the signal layer means editing that dict. tests/test_enrichment.py holds REGISTRABLE_SHAPE, REFERENCE_TABLE_SHAPE and LOAD_TABLE_SHAPE as the second copy of the three interfaces, asserted against the engine -- the same deliberate friction FLATTEN_SHAPES and HOST_CONTEXT_SHAPE have. (5) `helena.enrichment` is where the next loader goes, and the shape to copy is: fetch, parse COMPLETELY, then write; a typed PublicSuffixListError carrying one of three reasons; a frozen Pydantic load row that refuses a failure naming a snapshot or a success naming a reason; insert-then-FLUSH-then-delete-by-old-version; and the source URL through Redactor.url before it is stored as provenance. The redactor parameter is required rather than optional, deliberately. (6) The source URL lives in scripts/load_public_suffix_list.py and nowhere else -- the package may not hold one, and test_no_module_in_the_package_holds_a_broker_address is what enforces that. The next feed's URL belongs in its own script for the same reason. (7) The suite now makes two live HTTP requests to publicsuffix.org and skips them when the machine has no route. If a future session sees test_the_extract_answers_as_the_published_list_does fail, the committed 34-rule extract is stale and needs regenerating from the current snapshot -- that is what the failure means, not that the derivation is wrong. Untouched and still open from earlier sessions: bin/README.md's dangling reference to scripts/build-binaries.sh, and the two cross-cutting open questions in concept/08 (the record lost at a catch-up boundary, and durability for the single store).
